citation: Prast, E. J., Van de Weijer-Bergsma, E., Kroesbergen, E. H., & Van Luit, J. E. H. (2018). Differentiated instruction in primary mathematics: Effects of teacher professional development on student achievement. Learning and Instruction, 54, 22-34. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.learninstruc.2018.01.009
design: Cluster (school-level) RCT; 30 primary schools randomized to 3 cohorts (Cohort 1 = PD in Year 1 then follow-up; Cohort 2 = control Year 1, PD in Year 2; Cohort 3 = control both years); grades 1-6 (Mixed grade level); subject = mathematics; TPD = 2-year 'GROW' professional development programme teaching teachers to use the cycle of differentiation (flexible within-class ability grouping / differentiated instruction) in primary mathematics; control = business-as-usual mathematics teaching. N = 5658 students total (Year-1 analytic N = 4751; Year-2 analytic N = 4692). 196 classes (Year 1) / 186 classes (Year 2); avg class size 24. The Netherlands.
problems: EFFECT-SIZE METRIC IS NON-STANDARD (latent growth-curve model, not a posttest mean comparison). The authors analysed math achievement with latent growth-curve models (Mplus, type=complex for clustering) and modelled the PD effect on the SLOPE (rate of achievement growth over the school year), NOT on a posttest level. They explicitly do not interpret the intercept (level) effect. There is therefore no covariate-adjusted posttest mean/SD or posttest ANCOVA impact coefficient to standardize in the usual way. The extracted effect size is the authors' STANDARDIZED regression coefficient (beta) of the PD dummy on the latent slope (Table 5 Model 2 for Year 1; Table 7 Model 2 for Year 2), which is the covariate-adjusted standardized effect the meta-analysts would convert (Visscher et al. 2.5: 'effect sizes adjusted for pretest and other baseline covariates ... based on the statistics provided in the primary studies (e.g., F-tests, regression coefficients, means and SDs)'). g = J*beta. | RAW-MEAN ROUTE NOT VALID: the Cito CMT is a single vertically-scaled cross-grade 'competence score' (range 0-169 across grades 1-6), so its raw/total SD (Table 4: Maths T2 SD=30.18) is dominated by grade-level variance, which the growth model controls for via a grade-level covariate. Dividing the reported raw extra-growth of ~2.5 points (text p.29; avg growth 14.4 pts) by the total cross-grade SD gives a spuriously small d~0.08 that mixes within- and between-grade variance; it is NOT comparable to the within-grade standardized beta and is reported only as notes, not used. The proper within-grade standardizing SD pooled across grades is not tabulated, so raw means/SDs are left null. | CLUSTER ADJUSTMENT: assignment was at the SCHOOL level (30 schools); SEs come from an Mplus type=complex model with cluster-robust SEs at the CLASS level (students nested within classes; authors note grade level is neither purely individual nor purely class-level). This accounts for within-class clustering but is a cluster-robust single-level approach, not a full school-level multilevel model, and the betas/SEs are at the student scale. cluster_adjusted set true with this caveat; ICC NOT reported by the authors (left null - not guessed); n_clusters recorded as 30 schools (units of assignment). The Hedges (2007) school-level cluster correction the meta-analysts applied would still need an ICC, which the paper does not provide. | J small-sample correction computed conservatively with df = n_clusters-2 = 28 (J=0.9730); with student-level df J~1 and g~=beta. | TWO independent short-term (immediate post-intervention) contrasts exist (Cohort 1 in Year 1; Cohort 2 in Year 2) from two different cohorts; both extracted (Year 1 = primary headline result; Year 2 = secondary). The Year-2 long-term effect of PD-in-Year-1 (slope beta=-0.06, p=.665, n.s.) is a follow-up wave, not immediate post, so NOT extracted (noted). | SUBGROUPS: multiple-group models by achievement level (low/average/high) reported (Tables 6 & 8); Wald tests showed NO significant differential effects across achievement groups, so only the full-sample overall effects are extracted (subgroup rows omitted; is_full_sample stays true). | SOURCE: legal green/institutional OA - publisher version PDF from the Radboud University institutional repository (Radboud Repository, hdl.handle.net/2066/189803), hosted under Article 25fa of the Dutch Copyright Act; the article is also Bronze OA at the Elsevier/ScienceDirect landing page (free to read). No piracy site used. The Utrecht University DSpace bitstream is now JS-rendered and could not be fetched directly.

effect_sizes.arm_label: GROW differentiated-instruction PD programme vs business-as-usual (Cohort 1 PD in Year 1 vs Cohorts 2+3 control)
effect_sizes.test_name: Cito Mathematics Tests (CMT; national Dutch curriculum-based progress-monitoring tests, Janssen, Scheltens & Kraemer 2005), grade-level-appropriate version, vertically-scaled competence score
effect_sizes.timepoint: Post / end of Year 1 (immediate post-intervention; T1 baseline mid-Year-1, T2 intercept, T3 end-Year-1; PD effect on Year-1 growth slope)
effect_sizes.g_method: g = J*beta, where beta = standardized regression coefficient of the 'PD in Year 1' dummy on the latent math-achievement growth SLOPE from the overall latent growth-curve Model 2 (Table 5, p.29; beta=0.15, SE=0.04, p=.007), covariate-adjusted for grade level, nonverbal intelligence, verbal WM, and visual-spatial WM (and the T1 baseline within the growth model). beta is the within-grade standardized effect on growth rate (positive favours PD). J = 1-3/(4*df-1) = 0.9730 with df = n_clusters-2 = 28 (conservative cluster df); g = 0.9730*0.15 = 0.146. g_se = J*SE_beta = 0.9730*0.04 = 0.0389; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.001515. (With student-level df, J~1 and g~=0.15, g_se~=0.04.) Standardized by the model's student-level (within-grade, covariate-residual) SD implicit in the standardized beta.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 5 (Overall model Year 1, Model 2) p.29; text p.29 (beta=0.15, p=.007; ~2.5 CMT points more growth than control, avg growth 14.4); design Table 1 p.25; Ns Table 2 (Cohort 1 N Year1=1514; Cohorts 2+3 Year1 = 1370+1867=3237); analytic N=4751
effect_sizes.notes: Headline result: significant small positive short-term effect of the PD on Year-1 math-achievement growth in Cohort 1 (beta=0.15, p=.007). n_t = Cohort 1 Year-1 students (1514); n_c = Cohorts 2+3 Year-1 students (1370+1867=3237); overall analytic N=4751. Effect is on the GROWTH SLOPE, not posttest level (authors do not interpret the intercept/level effect). Raw cross-check (text p.29): Cohort 1 gained ~2.5 CMT points more than controls over Year 1 (avg growth 14.4 points); dividing by the total cross-grade CMT SD (30.18) would give a grade-confounded d~0.08 that is NOT comparable and is not used. Multiple-group model (Table 6): effect similar across achievement groups (low beta=0.12 p=.051, average beta=0.10 p=.040, high beta=0.12 p=.036); Wald tests n.s. for differential effects, so no subgroup rows extracted. ICC not reported; cluster-robust (type=complex, class-level) SEs.

effect_sizes.arm_label: GROW differentiated-instruction PD programme vs business-as-usual (Cohort 2 PD in Year 2 vs Cohorts 1+3 control)
effect_sizes.test_name: Cito Mathematics Tests (CMT; national Dutch curriculum-based progress-monitoring tests, Janssen, Scheltens & Kraemer 2005), grade-level-appropriate version, vertically-scaled competence score
effect_sizes.timepoint: Post / end of Year 2 (second independent immediate post-intervention contrast; T3 start, T4 intercept, T5 end-Year-2; PD effect on Year-2 growth slope)
effect_sizes.g_method: g = J*beta, where beta = standardized regression coefficient of the 'PD in Year 2' dummy (short-term effect) on the latent math-achievement growth SLOPE from the overall latent growth-curve Model 2 (Table 7, p.31; beta=0.03, SE=0.07, p=.640, n.s.), covariate-adjusted for grade level, nonverbal intelligence, verbal WM, and visual-spatial WM. J = 0.9730 (df = n_clusters-2 = 28); g = 0.9730*0.03 = 0.029. g_se = J*SE_beta = 0.9730*0.07 = 0.0681; g_var = 0.004639.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 7 (Overall model Year 2, Model 2) p.31; text p.30-31 ('PD in Year 2' short-term slope effect beta=0.03, p=.640, n.s.); Ns Table 2 (Cohort 2 N Year2=1408; Cohorts 1+3 Year2 = 1494+1790=3284); analytic N=4692
effect_sizes.notes: Second independent immediate post-intervention contrast (different cohort/year): the PD effect could NOT be replicated in Year 2 - no significant short-term effect on Year-2 growth slope (beta=0.03, p=.640). n_t = Cohort 2 Year-2 students (1408); n_c = Cohorts 1+3 Year-2 students (1494+1790=3284); overall analytic N=4692. Authors attribute the smaller Cohort-2 effect to lower school motivation, less-experienced teachers, and concurrent curriculum changes (discussion p.31). The Year-2 LONG-TERM effect of PD-in-Year-1 (Cohort 1) on the slope was also n.s. (beta=-0.06, p=.665) and is NOT extracted (follow-up wave, not immediate post). Multiple-group model Year 2 (Table 8): no significant short- or long-term effects in any achievement group. Same cluster-robust caveats and missing ICC as the Year-1 row.
